content: 1. The ART register includes information about the district and health facility where the patient is receiving care. 2. It records the specific antiretroviral therapy (ART) regimen the patient is on, categorized as first-line, second-line, or third-line regimens. 3. The ART start date is documented alongside a unique identification number for each patient. 4. Patient details such as clinic ID, surname, given name, sex, and age are recorded. 5. For female patients, pregnancy and breastfeeding status are noted. 6. Tuberculosis (TB) status and CD4 count (or percentage if the patient is under 5 years old) are also included. 7. The initiation date of cotrimoxazole (CTX) prophylaxis is recorded in terms of month and year. 8. Any history of previous TB treatment or other significant medical conditions is documented. 9. Registration and personal information are meticulously recorded, including pregnancy details. For each pregnancy, the expected delivery date (EDD), antenatal care (ANC) number, and HIV-exposed infant (HEI) number are noted. 10. The cohort year and month of ART initiation are specified. 11. The patient’s status at the start of ART is documented, with additional fields filled in as applicable. 12. The guidelines emphasize person-centered HIV patient monitoring and case surveillance. 13. Follow-up data is collected at specific intervals (e.g., months 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, etc.), including viral load, CD4 count (or percentage if under 5 years old), and follow-up status. 14. If the follow-up status is marked as STOP, the reasons for discontinuation are recorded, along with the duration of interruption and whether ART was restarted later. 15. A list is maintained of patients who may not or will not initiate ART soon after enrollment into HIV care. 16. For these patients, the date of enrollment into HIV care, unique ID number, clinic number, name, surname, given name, sex, age, baseline CD4 count, and TB history are documented.
